key_insight: Strong diagnostic performance did not translate into reliable downstream cancer care, with LLM failure patterns changing across care phases.
clinical_relevance: Evaluating medical LLMs across the care pathway may reveal errors and omissions that isolated diagnostic tests miss.
method: Introduced NPC-RubricBench using longitudinal nasopharyngeal carcinoma records from two cancer centers.
Assessed 30 general-purpose and medical LLMs across six care phases using patient-specific criteria and decision-time evidence only.
Compared phase-specific failures and the effects of broad versus checklist-like prompts.
evidence_signal: The benchmark included 405 patients, 941 patient-phase units and 17,688 criteria; decision errors dominated anatomical staging (48.2%), while omissions dominated initial work-up (33.4%) and post-treatment follow-up (30.4%).
watch_item: Checklist-like prompts improved Decision Quality but reduced Evidence Faithfulness and Safety Adherence, highlighting a trade-off rather than a universal prompting fix.
paper_title: Patient-specific rubric-based evaluation of large language models across longitudinal cancer care
